doc.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023

title: Where ideas come from: Math Camp and 'Hadron, Meson, Baryon'
summary: She explains how Frasier, Einstein and a science article led to the Math Camp album and the song.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well the leap from — you’ve made a few leaps. And before too much times goes by I want to ask you where your ideas come from. Because you’ve written everything from a song about bats in your apartment to this — I might as well just ask you about this song right now.
I saw this song title and — “Hadron, Meson, Baryon”

Thank you. I knew I’d mispronounce that but I thought, “Oh that’s interesting she wrote a song about a law firm.” So you know I did some digging and where did the idea to write about subatomic particles come from?

I don’t know where these ideas come from sometimes but I had — I was reading this book by Walter Isaacson, a terrific writer, Einstein: His Life and Universe. And I was thinking of this episode of “Frasier” my ex-husband used to play in the warm-up band for “Frasier” because it was done live. And there was a scene in which Frasier was going on a tropical vacation and his family was there and his latest girlfriend was there, and Frasier is just being a real jerk. He’s complaining about everything. And the girlfriend says, “Come on Frasier, can’t you just relax? Can’t you just have fun?” And he says, “Fun? Fun was my middle name in math camp.” So I did a little digging and I found out that math camp is a thing, and that you have to take a qualifying quiz. I don’t know anything about physics, I just thought I wanted to do an album called “Math Camp.” And so I went to various websites like Electromagnetism for Dummies and so forth, and I just picked up certain little words and phrases that I thought were cool. And the way that I wrote “Hadron, Meson, Baryon” was that I saw an article that I think it was in “The Atlantic” reprinted from “Quanta” magazine. But it was called “A Fight for the Soul of Science” and it had a photo of all of these physicists at a conference and the lead guy is older and he’s got his head in his hands like as if in despair. And the idea was that they, these people had thought maybe they should just team up with philosophers to try and figure out how it all started because the search to go ever smaller, smaller, smaller, smaller, and see what is the basis of everything can only go so far unless you have like a quadrillion

dollars. So they were just in despair. And then I saw these names of the elementary particles and I thought it was “mayson” too but I looked it up, Hadron, Meson, Baryon. And I thought well that’s kind of a hooky little — that would make a good hook. Hadron, Meson, Baryon. So I created a little story about a class of people who are in despair and they’re wondering what’s at the bottom of it all and the physicist in the story is a woman and she goes back and she’s with her husband. And you know it’s just — writing lyrics is so much fun, like I said well they should have a dog. There are more animals in my songs than normal I know. What kind of a dog would it be? And I picked out a Maltese mix, a mix, ‘cause I like to support the rescue efforts. But it just — and from there it’s hard to say, it just kind of evolved or blossomed.
